Alum and instructor Willie Castro achieves prestigious GM World Class Technician status
jobs.description: Cerritos College alum and instructor Willie Castro achieves prestigious GM World Class Technician status Printer-friendly version FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: May 27, 2026 Media Contact: Aya Aoki; Public Relations and Communications NORWALK, Calif. – May 27, 2026 – Cerritos College’s Automotive Mechanical Repair Instructor Willie Castro has earned the prestigious General Motors World Class Technician status. This esteemed recognition represents the highest level of excellence a GM technician can attain. The journey to becoming a World Class Technician is rigorous and demanding. Technicians must meet strict certification requirements through training programs offered by the GM Service Technical College and the National Institute for Automotive Service Excellence (ASE). The World Class Technician program allows technicians to validate their extensive knowledge and showcase their skills across various automotive service areas, earning them the title of “one and only GM expert.” Willie, a proud alumnus of the Cerritos College Automotive Mechanical Repair Program, has taught part-time at Cerritos College for over 20 years and has over 37 years of experience in the automotive industry. He also serves as a Field Service Engineer for General Motors and is an ASE Advanced Level Specialist with master certifications in Automotive and Medium/Heavy Truck Technician. His background includes work at GM and as a Master Diagnostic Technician for Audi, where he developed expertise in advanced diagnostics and electrical systems. At Cerritos College, he teaches in the GM ASEP Program, covering basic and advanced automotive systems, as well as electric vehicle (EV) systems and safety. "Congratulations to Willie for achieving General Motors World Class Technician status. Only about 7-8 percent of GM technicians reach this level, as the process is quite rigorous. In the United States, there are over 40,000 technicians, yet fewer than 3,000 have attained this honor. Willie is truly dedicated to preparing the next generation of automotive professionals with the essential skills needed for a technology-driven industry,” said Joe Mulleary, professor and chair of the Automotive Mechanical Repair program at Cerritos College. Cerritos College’s GM ASEP program has been a driving force in California’s workforce development since 1979, becoming a national model for equity-driven workforce transformation. Students benefit from advanced classroom instruction and participate in paid internships at local GM dealerships, where they gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge automotive technologies and build professional networks for high-demand jobs. The program was named a 2025 Examples of Excelencia award winner and a finalist in the 2026 Bellwether Awards. About Cerritos College: Cerritos College serves as a comprehensive community college for southeastern Los Angeles County. Communities within the college’s district include Artesia, Bellflower, Cerritos, Downey, Hawaiian Gardens, La Mirada, Norwalk, and portions of Bell Gardens, Lakewood, Long Beach, Santa Fe Springs and South Gate. Cerritos College offers nearly 300 degrees and certificates in nine divisions. Annually, more than 5,000 students successfully complete their course of studies, and enrollment currently averages 21,000 students. Visit Cerritos College online at www.cerritos.edu. -END-

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor of Clinical Neurological Surgery (Neuro - Oncologist)
jobs.description: Assistant or Associate Professor of Clinical Neurological Surgery (Neuro - Oncologist) Los Angeles, CA Apply Current employees apply here Job ID REQ20175743 Category Faculty Helpful Information for Applicants External Applicants Internal Applicants (Current USC Employees) Department of Neurological Surgery Faculty Los Angeles, CaliforniaThe University of Southern California (USC), founded in 1880, is the largest private employer in the City of Los Angeles. As an employee of USC, you will be a part of a world-class research university and a member of the “Trojan Family,” which is comprised of the faculty, students and staff that make the university what it is.The Department of Neurological Surgery is looking for an outstanding board eligible/board certified Neuro-Oncologist. The candidate will be fellowship trained and must be eligible for licensure in the State of California. This position is for an Assistant or Associate Professor of Clinical Neurological Surgery.The successful candidate will be expected to play an active role in the education of medical students, residents, and fellows in the areas of Neuro-Oncology. The successful candidate will develop and/or continue a record of scholarly accomplishment and participate in and/or develop clinical research programs in neuro-oncology, including investigator-initiated clinical trial protocols. The successful candidate will be expected to obtain independent funding to support investigator-initiated trials and related scholarly activities. In collaboration with relevant programs at Keck Medicine of USC and the USC Norris Comprehensive Cancer Center, the candidate will help develop scholarly programs and a well-balanced clinical trial portfolio that advances the care of patients with primary and metastatic brain and spinal cord tumors. The successful candidate will also work with relevant clinical and research programs to develop new clinical service lines that provide comprehensive, multidisciplinary care for patients with primary and metastatic brain and spinal cord tumors and neurological complications of cancer and cancer-directed therapies. In addition, the candidate will help establish standards of practice that promote efficient, safe, and coordinated patient care and facilitate clinical trial development, enrollment, and execution. The successful candidate will also participate in professional, public, and university service appropriate to the faculty rank.The position offers a competitive salary with excellent university benefits, and an academic appointment at the Keck School of Medicine of USC. The annual base salary range for this position is $275,000 – $400,000. When extending an offer of employment, the University of Southern California considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, federal, state, and local laws, contractual stipulations, grant funding, as well as external market and organizational considerations.Apply here and upload CV and 3 references. For further inquiries contact:William J. Qualified women and men, and members of all racial and ethnic groups, people with disabilities, and veterans are encouraged to apply.
